Vs. Naresh Kumar, thereby convicting and sentencing the appellant under Section 498A IPC for two years rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.5,000/-

3. Custody certificate dated 14.04.2024 issued by the Senior Superintendent, Central Jail, Agra tendered today is taken on record.
4. In the FIR lodged by Manoj Kumar, brother of the deceased Reena, it is mentioned that his sister was married with the appellant ten years as per Hindu rituals prior to the incident.

On 17.01.2011,
the appellant, his mother Anar Devi, sister-in-law Satyawati, Raj Kumari, Pushpa, Dewar Suresh and Sunny demanded Rs.50,000/- as additional dowry.
When the sister of the complainant refused to fulfil their demand, she was beaten by her husband, sister-in-law, mother-in-law and brother-in-laws and was locked the door from inside.
Kerosene oil was poured on her and she was burnt by igniting match.
All the accused ran away by opening the door.
The sister of the complainant raised alarm, on which neighbours came and informed the complainant about the incident.
When the complainant reached to his sister's house, his sister was found with 80% burn injuries and thereafter she was taken to the hospital.

5. Sister of the complainant was admitted in the Medical College, Agra and her dying declaration was recoded, in which she stated that on 17.01.2011 at 3'O clock her husband, Naresh demanded Rs.10,000/- - Rs.20,000/-, but she refused to fulfil the aforesaid demand.
Thereafter, an altercation took place between her and her husband and out of anger, her husband poured kerosene oil and ablazed her.
She further stated that her Dewar Sunny and Devrani Kalpana saved her and her mother-in-law also rebuked her husband.
On 23.01.2011, she died in the Heritage Hospital, Agra.
6. Written Tehrir was lodged on 18.01.2011 under Sections 498A and 302 IPC.
The investigation was conducted by the Investigating Officer by preparing site plan.
The inquest was conducted and thereafter post-mortem was also done by the Medical Officer, which is Ext.Ka-3.
After completing the investigation, charge sheet (Ext.Ka-11) was filed under Sections 498A and 302 IPC against the accused.
The learned Magistrate committed the case to the court of sessions and thereafter charges were framed in the aforesaid sections.
The accused denied the charges and pleaded for trial.

7. The prosecution to prove its case, produced the following seven witnesses:-
P.W.-1 Manoj Kumar P.W.-2 Om Prakash P.W.-3 Dr. Minesh Kumar Chawla P.W.-4 Dr. R.K. Kanchan P.W.-5 S.I. Yashpal Singh P.W.-6 Dr. Mohan Lal Arora P.W.-7 S.I.
Kishan Lal P.W.-8 S.I. Ghanshyam Singh P.W.-9
Vinod Kumr Sharma P.W.-10 Constable Rambhool Singh P.W.-11 Clerk Kanaiya Lal P.W.-12 Dharm Pal Singh P.W.-13 Dr. Rajiv Lochan Shrma 8.
The accused-appellant was confronted under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
He denied the charges and pleaded before the court that he was falsely implicated in the case.

The accused-appellant further produced D.W.-1 Km. Kumkum, daughter of the deceased and on the basis of the statement of D.W.-1, he also pleaded before the Court that he was falsely implicated and was liable to be acquitted.

sentences.text: P.W.-1, Manoj Kumar, bother of the deceased, has deposed the same facts in examination-in-chief as has been narrated in the FIR.
He, however, deposed in cross-examination that when he reached to the Sasural of his sister, he found that his sister was in burnt condition and she was taken by him to the S.N. Hospital.
Thereafter, she was shifted to the Heritage Hospital, Agra.
However, in cross-examination, he deposed that his sister was not burnt by her husband and in-laws and further denied demand of additional dowry by them.
P.W.-1 has been declared hostile after looking to his statement in cross-examination.
Similarly, P.W.-2 Om Prakash, father of the deceased, has also been declared hostile as he has not supported the prosecution case.

P.W.-3 Dr. Minesh Kumar Chawla was examined by the trial court and he proved the post-mortem report of the deceased, which is as follows:-
1.Symptoms of deep burn all over body except back of chest, abdomen, vaginal region, both Gols 2. symptoms of scalp hair present."
Cause of death is due to shock as a result of ante-mortem burn injuries.
10. P.W.-4
Dr. R.K. Kanchan was examined before the trial court and she deposed that dying declaration of the deceased was recorded by Vinod Kumar Sharma ACM-II, Agra.
She further deposed that she had given the fitness certificate to the extent that the deceased was able to make her statement before the ACM-II, Agra.

11. P.W.-5 S.I. Yashpal Singh, P.W.-6 Dr. Mohan Lal Arora, P.W.-7 S.I. Kishan Lal, P.W.-8 S.I.
Ghanshyam Singh, P.W.-9 Vinod Kumar Sharma, P.W.-10 Constable Rambhool Singh and P.W.-11 Clerk Kanaiya Lal are the formal witnesses, who have proved the documents.

12. P.W.-6 Dr. Mohan Lal Arora deposed before the Court that the deceased was brought in the hospital on 17.01.2011 and she was burnt upto 80-90% and there was smell of kerosene oil from the body of the deceased.

P.W.-9, Vinod Kumar Sharma, retired Deputy Collector was also examined before the trial court and he proved the dying declaration and deposed before the Court that after getting the fitness certificate, he recorded the statement of the deceased.
13.
The trial court after examining the witnesses and adducing the evidence on record, convicted the accused-appellant as mentioned above.
Hence, the present appeal has been filed.

14. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that P.W.1, Manoj Kumar, brother of the deceased,
and P.W.-2 Om Prakash, father of the deceased, have been declared hostile and, therefore, it cannot be construed that the accused-appellant was involved in commission of crime.
He further submits that P.Ws.1 and 2 have denied the charge of demand of additional dowry.
He also submits that the deceased was burnt upto 80-90%, thus she was not in a condition to give her statement.
The FIR indicates the date of incident is 21.01.2011, whereas the incident took place on 17.01.2011.
He further submits that the appellant also got burn injuries while saving the deceased and he himself had taken her to the hospital.

Lastly, it has been submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant Naresh Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67498522/

She further stated that her father and uncle tried to save her mother.

15. In support of his contention, learned counsel for the appellant has placed reliance upon a judgement of the Hon'ble Supreme Court rendered in the case of Kalu Ram Vs. State of Rajasthan,
(2000) 10 SCC 324.
16.

Kalu Ram Vs. State of Rajasthan,
(2000) 10 SCC 324

sentences.text: Learned AGA while rebutting the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that looking to the dying declaration of the deceased, it is evident that she has levelled clear allegation against the appellant and has stated that her husband poured kerosene oil and ablazed her as she could not fulfil the demand of additional dowry.
Learned AGA has further pointed out that D.W.-1 Km. Kumkum is the real daughter of the appellant and she has been won over by the appellant because she is dependent on him.
He has further submitted that the prosecution is able to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt and, therefore, the conviction and sentence awarded by the trial court needs no interference.

17. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and going through the record as well as the impugned judgement and order, we find that the deceased had given her dying declaration before the ACM-II, Agra.
The deceased stated before the Magistrate that her husband used to demand Rs.10,000/- - Rs.20,000/- usually.
She was married in 2000 and till the incident, she had given him Rs.40,000/- - Rs.50,000/-.
She could not fulfil his demand continuously and on the date of incident, there was altercation between her and her husband as he was demanding money.
Her husband poured kerosene oil and ablazed her.
She further deposed that her Dewar Sunny and Devrani Kalpana tried to save her.
Her mother-in-law also rebuked her husband and tried to save her.

It is true that P.Ws.1 and 2 have been declared hostile, but they have not seen the incident,
rather they were present at their own house.
Further, dying declaration of the deceased cannot be disbelieved.
The appellant committed crime by pouring kerosene oil and ablazing his wife, which is supported by dying declaration.
18. Statement of D.W.-1 Km. Kumkum, who is the daughter of the deceased and the appellant cannot be relied upon.
It is important to note that being daughter she was dependant on the appellant, therefore, she could not have courage to give statement against her father.
At the time of trial, she was eleven years old and whatever she was taught by her grand parents, she told before the trial court.

19. So far the augment of learned counsel for the appellant that the deceased was brunt upto 80-90%, therefore, she was unable to give her statement, cannot be accepted as the doctor had given the fitness certificate and thereafter her statement was recorded before the ACM-II, Agra.

The doctor as well as ACM-II, Agra were produced before the court and they had stated before the trial court that the dying declaration was recorded before them.
20.
So far the argument of learned counsel for the appellant that the FIR is ante-timed, is also not sustainable as the FIR has been lodged on 21.01.2011 and the Written Tehrir is dated 18.01.2011.

sentences.text: However, there is cutting on the date for the simple reason that FIR was lodged on 21.01.2011; thus no adverse inference can be drawn.
21. After discussing the evidence on record, we are of the opinion that the appellant committed the offence by pouring kerosene oil on the body of the deceased and thereafter ablazed her.

However,
the dying declaration indicates that there was altercation between the appellant and the deceased as the appellant demanded money from the deceased, which she refused and admittedly she has mentioned that her husband suddenly became angry and thereafter poured kerosene oil and ablazed her.
The aforesaid act of the appellant indicates that out of grave and sudden provocation, he committed the offence.
He asked his wife to give money and she refused, on which he became so angry and committed the offence.

Similar facts have been taken into consideration by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kalu Ram (supra) and after considering the entire facts and circumstances and the evidence, Hon'ble Supreme Court alter the conviction and sentence of the appellant therein under Section 302 IPC to Section 304 Part-II IPC.

The relevant paragraphs of the aforesaid judgement are extracted herein blow:-
"7.
But then, what is the nature of the offence proved against him.
It is an admitted case that appellant was in a highly inebriated stage when he approached the deceased when the demand for sparing her ornaments was made by him.
When she refused to oblige he poured kerosene on her and wanted her to lit the match-stick.
When she failed to do so he collected the match box and ignited one match-stick but when flames were up he suddenly and frantically poured water to save her from the tongues of flames.
This conduct cannot be seen divorced from the totality of the circumstances.
Very probably he would not have anticipated that the act done by him would have escalated to such a proportion that she might die.
If he had ever intended her to die he would not have alerted his senses to bring water in an effort to rescue her.

We are inclined to think that all what the accused thought of was to inflict burns to her and to frighten her but unfortunately the situation slipped out of his control and it went to the fatal extent.
He would not have intended to inflict the injuries which she sustained on account of his act.
Therefore, we are persuaded to bring down the offence from the first degree murder to culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
8. We, therefore, alter the conviction from Section 302, I.P.C. to Section 304, Part II of the I.P.C.
Both sides conceded that appellant is continuing in jail.
We impose a sentence of rigorous imprisonment for seven years on him.

It is for the jail authorities to count whether the period he had already undergone would be sufficient to complete the period of sentence imposed by us and if so, the jail authorities shall release him from jail.
Otherwise he will continue in jail until completion of the period of seven years of imprisonment.
The appeal is disposed of accordingly."

sentences.text: In the present case also, we see that admittedly there was altercation between the deceased and the appellant and suddenly out of anger, the appellant poured kerosene oil and ablazed her.
It has also come on record that the appellant had also received burn injuries while saving the deceased.
It appears that the appellant tried to save her later on, but due to serious burn injuries, she died.

23. Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case; the mitigating factors; the fact that P.Ws.1, Manoj Kumar, brother of the deceased, and P.W.-2, Om Prakash, father of the deceased,
have been declared hostile and D.W.-1, Km. Kumkum, daughter of the deceased also did not support the prosecution case, we alter the sentence and conviction of the appellant of the offence under Section 302 read with 498-A IPC to Section 304 Part-I IPC and sentenced him for a period of ten years rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.1,000/-.

24. The custody report dated 14.04.2024 indicates that the appellant had already undergone 13 years and five moths actual custody including custody during trial and 16 years of total sentence including remission.

25. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed and the impugned judgement and order dated 14.08.2013 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.17, Agra in Sessions Trial No.387 of 2011, arising out of Case Crime No.40 of 2011, is modified to the extent that conviction and sentence awarded by the trial court under Section 302 IPC is altered to Section 304 Part-I IPC for ten years rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.1,000/-.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.17, Agra
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The conviction and sentence awarded by the trial court to the appellant under Section 498-A IPC is upheld, however, the fine imposed under Section 498A IPC is reduced to Rs.500/-.
We have reduced the fine because the appellant has served out three years more than the actual period of sentence awarded by this Court.

26. Since both the sentences i.e. under Sections 498A and 302 IPC run concurrently, therefore,
accused-appellant Naresh is entitled to be released from jail on the ground that he has already undergone the period of sentence in jail as awarded by this Court.
27. Appellant-Naresh is in jail.
He shall be set at liberty forthwith.
He need not surrender unless wanted in any other case.
The fine imposed by this Court shall be deposited within a period of two months from the date of his release.

28. Let lower court record be sent back forthwith along with a copy of this judgement and order for compliance.
.
(Brij Raj Singh, J.) (Siddharth, J.) Order Date :- 15.7.2024 Rao/-
